name: Taiwan 2050
description: Net zero without nuclear, as in the Taiwan energy model: 80 GW of solar, 61 GW of mostly offshore wind, geothermal, gas with carbon capture, ammonia turbines and hydrogen peakers. Sunset is still the hard part.
dataNotes: Solar, wind, geothermal, biomass, hydro, coal and oil come from the Taiwan energy model's main 2050 run (official options, all imports, no new nuclear; PyPSA-Earth, daily steps, results of 2026-09-26). Gas and ammonia come from the same run with 4-hour steps (official_imp_4h), which sees the evening peak: 18.3 GW of gas and 14.3 GW of ammonia combined cycle, each plus 15% as a planning reserve for outages, maintenance and hot weather (Taiwan's reserve margin target), so 21.0 GW of gas and 16.4 GW of ammonia. All gas combined cycles (19.3 GW, including the model's 1.2 GW of gas CHP) capture 95% of their CO₂; the gas peakers (1.7 GW) burn imported hydrogen. Coal (4 GW) is kept as a reserve that the model hardly uses. Batteries use the official 5.5 GW target (4 hours); the model's 60 GW of vehicle-to-grid is left out. Demand is the model's 2050 electricity generation (471 TWh). The model grows electricity demand mainly for electronics (chip fabs, data centres), which run around the clock, so the growth over 2025 (about 180 TWh, 20.6 GW) is a flat load on top of the 2025 load shape (40.75 GW peak): peak load 61.35 GW. Unit counts and all unit parameters are illustrative.
